description: You are a Healthcare IT Integration Specialist at a reference laboratory that receives nightly batch HL7 files from 12 hospital clients. Each batch file contains multiple HL7 messages wrapped in BHS/BTS (Batch Header/Trailer Segment) envelope. The current manual processing creates a 4-hour backlog each morning. Build a NextGen Connect channel named 'Nightly HL7 Batch Processor' that: (1) Uses a File Reader source connector (NOT a TCP Listener) that polls the directory /home/ga/hl7_batch_inbox/ for files matching the pattern *.hl7 every 30 seconds. (2) Contains a JavaScript preprocessor (not a regular transformer - use the Preprocessor script area in the channel) that splits the batch file: iterates through the batch content, strips BHS/BTS envelope segments, and splits the content into individual HL7 messages by detecting segment boundaries, returning an array of individual messages. Alternatively, configure the channel with batch processing enabled and a custom batch script. (3) Uses a Database Writer destination that INSERTs each processed message record into a PostgreSQL table 'batch_processing_log' with columns: batch_file VARCHAR(255), message_seq INTEGER, patient_mrn VARCHAR(50), message_type VARCHAR(20), processed_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(). The channel should extract patient MRN from PID-3 and message type from MSH-9. (4) After processing, the File Reader should be configured to MOVE processed files to /home/ga/hl7_batch_archive/ (use the 'After Processing Action' = Move setting). (5) The channel must be deployed. A sample batch file is pre-placed at /home/ga/hl7_batch_inbox/nightly_batch_20240115.hl7. Create the required directories and table before or during setup. PostgreSQL: jdbc:postgresql://nextgen-postgres:5432/mirthdb (user: postgres, password: postgres). Direct: docker exec nextgen-postgres psql -U postgres -d mirthdb. REST API: https://localhost:8443/api (admin:admin). All API calls require header: X-Requested-With: OpenAPI.
